target: the forecast outturn now stands 7 weeks behind the approved programme. The cause is rework of issued-for-construction drawings: a late design change left errors in drawings already issued for the EPC packages, and the errors came to light through fabrication queries, after fabrication slots had been booked against the original issue dates. Released slots and out-of-sequence procurement have moved the delay beyond the drawings office; packages previously ahead of their need dates now press against them. One mitigation is proposed. The remaining work is resequenced so that fabrication and construction proceed first on the packages whose drawings are complete and checked, and the packages under rework are held until their drawings are reissued and independently verified. The project board owns the recovery plan: the board reviews progress against the revised sequence and authorises the additional checking resource the drawings office needs. The revised sequence is built package by package from the drawing register, so that each package carries its own status: drawings complete, drawings under rework, or drawings not yet issued. Packages in the first group move forward without restriction. Packages under rework are reissued in the order the fabrication shops can absorb them, and no package in that group is released on partial information, since a second round of rework on the same package would cost more than the wait for a complete reissue. Site works that do not depend on the reworked drawings, such as foundations and underground services, continue on their existing dates, and the delay is thereby contained within the packages the design change touched. Resequencing protects the unaffected packages and keeps the fabrication shops loaded, and it does not recover the full delay, because the reissued drawings still pass through fabrication in their turn and the packages they serve finish late by the time the rework itself consumed.
